clue.text: Fuel company with a shortfall finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word shortfall

explanation.surface: A fuel firm is running short of supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a fossil fuel burned for heat and power.

clue.text: Rambling up to cafe to get a hot drink

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone strolls up to a café for a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of tea is the quintessential British hot beverage.

clue.text: Top chap expecting traps

indicators.note: traps means catches or holds, so the phrase chap expecting holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A leading man anticipates being snared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traps' looks like the noun the chap expects, but it is the verb: the words 'chap expecting' catch the answer inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or summit of something.

clue.text: Song in church provided by a new boy

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A church hymn is supplied by a new choirboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanson is a French song, especially a cabaret or art song.

clue.text: Lad underneath vehicle shows bottle

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece underneath another follows it, so the lad comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy lying under a car reveals a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large rounded glass or plastic bottle, often encased, used for liquids such as acids.

clue.text: Gathering in university entertained by comical aunt dancing

indicators.note: something entertained by a host is taken in, so the university letter sits inside the other letters
dancing letters move about, so comical aunt is jumbled

explanation.surface: At a university gathering a comical aunt is dancing for the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles COMICAL AUNT and 'entertained by' puts U inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An accumulation is a build-up or collection, a gathering of things over time.

clue.text: One sober person in view to avoid action

indicators.note: in places the one and the sober person inside the word for view

parts.note: sight can mean view, as in 'in sight'
I is the Roman numeral for one
TT means teetotal, so a teetotaller, a sober person

explanation.surface: A lone teetotaller stays in view, keeping out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, is a crossword staple for someone who does not drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is an idiom for staying put and not taking any action.

clue.text: Signal before entrance to every junction

parts.note: a nod is a signal given with the head

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter, here of every

explanation.surface: A sign is given before entering every road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a point where lines or branches meet, a connecting point.

clue.text: Supporters of wicked things

parts.note: read 'wicked' not as evil but as having a wick: the holders for such things

explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like 'evil', making the supporters villains' allies; it really means 'having wicks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlesticks hold up candles, which are objects with wicks.

clue.text: Ready-made red carpet I supply, brilliant for inside

indicators.note: for inside says the word for brilliant goes into the middle of the jumbled letters
supply here is the adverb, in a supple way, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means brilliant

explanation.surface: A shop offers a ready-made red carpet, fine for indoor use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb, but it is the adverb of supple, flexing RED CARPET I; 'for inside' puts FAB within.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefabricated parts are built in advance in a factory, ready for assembly.

clue.text: Couple turning noisy, left out

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for left is removed
turning means the word for noisy is read backwards

parts.note: loud means noisy

explanation.surface: A pair grow rowdy and are excluded from the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' turns LOUD into DUOL; 'out' then drops L.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of people, especially performers.

clue.text: Time to meet French friend, someone learning language

parts.note: ami is French for friend
L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: It is time for a learner to meet a French pal for language practice.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are the plates marking a learner driver in Britain, hence L for a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian language spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: A good measure introduced by fellow who went on long expedition?

definitions.note: the definition describes a person; the clue's 'fellow' doubles as the subject

indicators.note: introduced by means taken inside, so the first pieces go into the word for fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A man takes a good measure of things on a long voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'fellow' too: the fellow who went on a long expedition. An ell was an old cloth measure of about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to sail round the world.

clue.text: Junior tearaway, ultimately having no urge to reform

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of tearaway
to reform means to form again, so the letters of no urge are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young tearaway, in the end, has no wish to mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior means lower in age, so a younger person.

clue.text: Herd suffering with encroaching river given new shelter

indicators.note: encroaching means intruding, so the river pushes into the middle of the jumbled letters
suffering herd letters are knocked about and rearranged

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A suffering herd, flooded by a river, is moved to fresh shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' jumbles the herd into REHD for 'encroaching' to break open. The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse is to provide with new accommodation.

clue.text: Month to go to a golf course in America

parts.note: August is a month

explanation.surface: Someone spends a month at an American golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta National in Georgia hosts the Masters golf tournament.

clue.text: NW state unfortunately ends with black lava

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

indicators.note: ends picks the final letter of each of the words black and lava

explanation.surface: Sadly, a volcanic eruption concludes with black lava.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' looks like an anagram signal but gives ALAS; 'ends' then takes the last letters of 'black' and 'lava'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the US state in the far north-west of the continent.

clue.text: Admirer's initial longing to construct a letter

indicators.note: initial points to the opening letter of the word Admirer's

parts.note: an itch is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: An admirer feels an urge to compose a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a letter' looks like correspondence; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H.

clue.text: Fate of some plotters

indicators.note: of some means part of the word plotters provides the answer

explanation.surface: This is the destiny awaiting certain conspirators.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny or fortune in life.

clue.text: Beast turning up — turning up in the morning

indicators.note: turning, in a down clue, flips the word up so it reads upward
turning up repeats the instruction, so the morning abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A wild animal keeps showing up at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'turning' reverses UP into PU; 'turning up' then flips AM to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A puma is a big wild cat, also called cougar or mountain lion.

clue.text: Model again getting embarrassed over nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the colour comes before the nothing

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sculptor reworks a model, flushing over a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo is to make or fashion something a second time.

clue.text: Cruel guys Tom's mistaken for bad people

indicators.note: mistaken suggests the letters of the phrase are in a wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Tom's harsh companions are taken for villains.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly customer is an idiom for a nasty or threatening person.

clue.text: A name is confused, memory being lost

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddling up a name hints at a fading memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for loss of memory.

clue.text: Bishop, experienced and fearless

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
old can mean experienced, as in an old hand

explanation.surface: A seasoned bishop is courageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold means brave and daring, without fear.
